The #MeToo Movement took the world by storm, country by country. But we still don’t talk about the importance of intersectionality within it. Patriarchy affects all of us, no matter our gender and sexual identity, no matter where we come from. (1/7)

And when it comes to the #MeToo movement, and assault, people within the queer community are not only attacked by people who are homophobic, but also by people within the community itself- partners, friends, family. 
(4/7)

This is why understanding and working with #intersectionality is important- there is never one kind of person who goes through one kind of violence. People through the layers of society have all kinds of different needs, based on their identities.

#QueerToo within the #MeToo

Violence does occur in the community. But there are various reasons that stop queer people from talking about this violence.
Let's talk about why.
#MeToo #QueerToo #amplifyqueervoices

But for now, this is a primer/ peek into what changes when we talk about the queer movement within the #metoo movement. Please feel free to ask us questions here, or even on Gaysi Family on all Social Media!

#queertoo within the #metoo

Also, special thanks to @IndiaMeToo for doing what an ally should- amplifying queer voices by having queer folx speak! 

#queertoo #metoo #LGBTQ

Genuine ques: How have you changed your own behaviour post #MeToo to ensure that you aren’t enabling patriarchy? What steps have you taken to make women around you feel safer? What kind of introspection have you done? Positive steps taken? Do you listen more? Would love to know.
